items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: AC-1..AC-6 implemented. AC-2's guard was moved INTO the executable snippet after the external plan review; AC-6 drives the shipped hooks.json chain rather than a hand-assembled one, so it cannot certify a composition nobody ships. AC-5 was initially under-delivered (see Documentation Honesty).

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: Wrapper covers producer timeout, unstartable producer, undocumented exit code, non-Shipwright tree, and a producer missing from a partial cache. Returns 0 on every path because the chain propagates the first non-zero child code. KeyboardInterrupt is deliberately NOT swallowed (except Exception, never BaseException), with a test pinning it.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: Producer driven as a fixed argv list, shell=False, no interpolation of project/repo values into a command string. Child stdout+stderr are captured and never echoed: gh error text is exactly where a token or auth header would surface, and the chain re-emits child stderr verbatim.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: 19 tests asserting outcomes (exit codes, stdout/stderr emptiness, argv shape, cwd, card counts) rather than internals. Track 1 confirmed red first; the one vacuous pass was given an explicit non-vacuity assert. Idempotency across sessions is proven by running the producer three times and asserting one card, not assumed from the dedup key.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: verify_local.py measured 8.4s against F0's multi-minute suite, and is ordered before it so it fails fast. Producer measured 1.5s + 3 gh calls per session, bounded by a 45s timeout so a stalled gh cannot hold session start open.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: New wrapper 168/300 LOC; three new test files 138-215/300. No changed file carries a bloat baseline entry, so nothing ratchets. The in-code alternative was rejected on measurement: run_test_suite.py is 518 against a baseline current of 518, i.e. zero headroom.

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: hooks.json (io boundary + cross_component), a new shared/scripts/hooks/*.py, two shipped runtime prompts (SKILL.md, F0.md), three docs, one docstring. Integration coverage drives the real run_if_cache_ready.py chain, which is the composition the cross_component flag demands.

items.name: Documentation Honesty
items.note: CAUGHT AND FIXED, not clean first time. The stale 'nothing invokes it for you' claim lived in THREE files; I corrected two and wrote the honesty test over the same two, so gate and defect shared a blind spot. The spec-reviewer found the third (docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md) — the file AC-5 explicitly enumerates. Fixed; test now covers all three; a repo-wide sweep confirmed no fourth home. guide.md 2.10 step 5 also corrected.

items.name: Cross-Platform Execution
items.note: The first F0 snippet was bash-only on a repo developed on Windows, where 'if [ -f ]' is a syntax error — a step that silently would not run on the primary platform, which is the exact failure this card is about. Both spellings now ship (the install-hooks.sh/.ps1 precedent) and both were probed empirically in both directions. The PowerShell branch captures $LASTEXITCODE and re-raises, so it can STOP the run as the bash block does.
